en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Twenty-Second Chapter
Discussion on Wholesome Consciousness:
Does an Arahant who possesses a wholesome consciousness attain final Nibbāna? Yes.
An arahant, while performing a volitional formation of merit...
while performing a volitional formation of the imperturbable...
while performing karma leading to a destination...
While performing karma that leads to existence… while performing karma that leads to sovereignty… while performing karma that leads to lordship…
While performing karma that leads to great wealth… while performing karma that leads to a large retinue… while performing karma that leads to divine beauty…
Does one who performs karma leading to human good fortune attain final Nibbāna?
One should not say so… [and so on] … Does an Arahant with a wholesome mind attain final Nibbāna?
“Yes.

[The opponent asks: “Does an arahant, while accumulating, while diminishing, while abandoning, while grasping, while breathing out, while breathing in, while shaking off, while blowing away, and while dispersing, attain final nibbāna?
“One should certainly not say so…” [and so on].
Is it not the case that the Arahant neither accumulates nor diminishes, but stands having already diminished [the defilements]?
Yes, it is so.
If the Arahant neither accumulates nor diminishes, but stands having already diminished [them], then indeed, you should not say: [that he is still accumulating].
“The Arahant, with a wholesome mind, attains final Nibbāna.
Is it not the case that the Arahant neither abandons nor clings, but stands having abandoned; neither sinks down nor rises up, but stands having sunk down;
and that the Arahant neither fans out nor fans in, but stands having fanned out?
“Yes,” [you say].
But if an Arahant neither fans out nor fans in, but stands having fanned out, then surely you should not say:
“An Arahant with a wholesome mind attains final Nibbāna.”
Is it not to be said that an Arahant with a wholesome mind attains final Nibbāna?
Yes, it is.
Is it not the case that an Arahant, with mindfulness established, mindful and clearly comprehending, attains final Nibbāna? Yes.
If an Arahant, with mindfulness established, mindful and clearly comprehending, attains final Nibbāna, then indeed, sir, you must say this:
“The Arahant, with a wholesome mind, attains final Nibbāna.
The Discussion on the Wholesome Mind is finished.
